cover.title: The call you're losing every Friday at 4pm
cover.subtitle: Older pipes in local neighborhoods don't wait for Monday morning.

slides.heading: The Friday afternoon rush
slides.body: It is late Friday in the East End. An old cast-iron stack backs up just as the homeowner starts cooking dinner.

slides.heading: Why they hang up
slides.body: If your hands are under a sink in Shaler and voicemail picks up, they rarely leave a message. They call the next shop on the list.
slides.tip: Call your own line after 5pm. What happens?

slides.heading: Catching the weekend work
slides.body: Answering right away lets you lock down the emergency before your competitors even see the missed notification.
slides.tip: Say: "I can get a tech there. Want that slot?"

slides.heading: Quick weekend capture
slides.body: Answer every late-week call, book the emergency straight into the calendar, and head into the weekend knowing your schedule is full.
slides.tip: Forward emergency lines to the on-call tech by 3:30pm every Friday.

caption:
Older Pittsburgh houses love to break things right when your team is wrapping up for the week.

When a main stack backs up on a Friday evening, homeowners will not wait around for a callback on Monday morning. They just dial the next number.

Setting up clear on-call rotations or dedicated call routing ensures emergency jobs stay on your board instead of going to competitors.
